headline: Hamburg have won 3 straight, yet Paderborn stay narrow favourites
summary: Hamburg arrive at Paderborn on a run of 3 straight Bundesliga wins, the latest 1-0 at home to Stuttgart. Yet the market does not make them favourites. Paderborn sit 16th of 18 and drew 2-2 at Werder Bremen on Saturday. Hamburg's problem is at the other end: 13 goals conceded in their last 5. Across 6 bookmakers, with the margin removed, Paderborn win 39.7% of the time and Hamburg 34.0%. The total-goals line is 3.0, so an open game is expected.
read: Paderborn are 16th and under pressure after letting a 2-0 lead slip at Werder Bremen, but the market still makes them narrow home favourites over a Hamburg side on a three-match winning run. The goal line sits at 3.0 because both defences have leaked all season, and a level handicap says the market rates the two teams as evenly matched.

facts.fact: Paderborn are narrow home favourites at 39.7% to win, with Hamburg at 34.0%.
facts.meaning: The market sees a near-even game in which home advantage only just beats the table gap between the sides.

facts.fact: Hamburg have won their last three Bundesliga matches, most recently 1-0 at home to Stuttgart.
facts.meaning: They arrive as clearly the form team of the two, after a dreadful opening to the season.

facts.fact: Hamburg have conceded 13 goals in their last five Bundesliga matches.
facts.meaning: Their winning run has papered over a defence that has been taken apart twice in that spell.

facts.fact: Paderborn sit 16th of 18 in the Bundesliga table.
facts.meaning: They are in the bottom three places and need a home result; the German press this week described them as under pressure.

facts.fact: Paderborn led 2-0 at Werder Bremen on Saturday and were pegged back to 2-2.
facts.meaning: Dropping points from two goals up leaves them without a win in three and turns this home game into a pressured one.

facts.fact: The main total-goals line is set at 3.0, with over and under split almost exactly evenly.
facts.meaning: The market expects an open game — three goals is the 50/50 point, well above a typical Bundesliga line.

facts.fact: Paderborn are conceding 2.04 expected goals per game over their last five while creating 1.01.
facts.meaning: They are being out-chanced roughly two to one, which is why they cannot pull clear of the bottom of the table.

facts.fact: The handicap fair line is -0.12 in Paderborn's favour, with the main line set at level (0).

sources.fact: Paderborn are under pressure going into the match, having drawn 2-2 with Werder Bremen after leading 2-0.
29 of Paderborn's 30 senior squad players trained on Wednesday, with only Oliver Batista Meier absent.
Nyamekye Awortwie-Grant has completed his first full training session with Paderborn in several months as he steps up his comeback.
Paderborn led 2-0 at Werder Bremen but were pegged back to 2-2, a result that highlighted the promoted side's remaining weaknesses.
Rayan Philippe, who celebrates his 26th birthday on Friday, faces his former club HSV on Saturday.
Steffen Tigges made his first Paderborn start in eight months at Bremen and rewarded the choice by scoring.
Hamburger SV are on a three-match winning run, which they aim to extend at Paderborn.
Albert Sambi Lokonga has resumed full training after a muscular problem and is on track to return to the HSV squad against Paderborn, though he may not start immediately.
